source_refs.note: Topic 17.9 as printed with Example 17.5 (PDF 98, printed 94). The heading is printed 'IMPENDANCE'.

blocks.text: In AC circuits, the opposition to current flow is called impedance denoted by Z, which includes both resistance R and reactance X. The resistance R is the opposition to current flow due to resistors. Reactance is the opposition to current flow due to capacitors (capacitive reactance X_C) and inductors (inductive reactance X_L). A pure resistive circuit has only resistance R and no reactance.

blocks.title: Impedance
blocks.text: The combined effect of resistance and reactances in such circuits is known as impedance.
It is the ratio of the rms value of the voltage to the rms value of the current. Thus,
This SI unit of impedance is ohm.

blocks.title: Example 17.5
blocks.problem: An AC circuit operates by a peak voltage of 200 V and 10 A as peak input current. Find the impedance of the circuit.
steps: Peak voltage Vₒ = 200 V, Peak current Iₒ = 10 A
We know that; Vᵣₘₛ = Vₒ × 0.707 = 200 V × 0.707 = 141.4 V
